source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's PNW1 campus in Quincy, Washington publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 720,000 square feet of technical space, and that is the whole specification.

The 36 MW is a power figure, not a rack count. At 40 kW per rack it implies roughly 900 racks, at 100 kW per rack roughly 360, and both are arithmetic applied to the published number rather than anything CyrusOne states. The 720,000 square feet is large enough that power, not floor area, is the likely constraint on how much compute the building holds, though no density figure is published to confirm it.

Within Washington, PNW1 ranks first by published megawatt capacity among the two facilities in the state that publish any figure. The state total of published capacity is 60 MW, so this campus accounts for 36 of the 60, with the remaining 24 MW at one other site. Against 46 mapped facilities in Washington, only two publish a number, so the ranking reflects disclosure rather than size.

The data carries no address, no postal code, and no certifications. The missing certifications say nothing about what the building is qualified to host, only that the operator's spec page does not list them. Nothing here establishes when the campus was built, how it is cooled, or what it draws from the grid beyond the IT load it advertises.
